unit.title: Perform basic testing and inspection on electrical installations

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why is a new installation inspected and tested before it is put into use?
options: To find out how much the customer must pay for it
To check it is safe and meets the standards
To find out how long the cables will last
To see how much power the house will use

questions.stem: When is the visual inspection done?
options: After all the live tests are finished
Only if a test result is bad
After the power company has connected the supply
Before testing, with the installation isolated

questions.stem: What is the usual order of the dead tests on a new installation?
options: Polarity, insulation resistance, continuity
Insulation resistance, polarity, continuity
Continuity, insulation resistance, polarity
Polarity, continuity, insulation resistance

questions.stem: Why is the continuity of protective conductors tested before insulation resistance?
options: Later tests rely on a sound earth path
It is the quickest test to do
It uses the highest test voltage
It must always be done with the supply switched on

questions.stem: When are live tests, such as earth fault loop and GFCI trip tests, carried out?
options: Before any of the dead tests are done
At the same time as the visual inspection
Instead of the dead tests, to save time
Only after the dead tests are passed

questions.stem: Which information do you need before you start testing an installation?
options: The customer's bank and payment details
The drawings and circuit details
The make of each appliance the customer owns
The dates on which the house was last painted

questions.stem: Before you use a test instrument, what should you check?
options: Its leads, probes and battery, and its calibration date
That it is the newest and most expensive tester in the store
That its case is the same colour as the panel
That it was used on the last job

questions.stem: Which test probes are the safest to use on electrical installations?
options: Long bare metal tips without any finger guards at all
Crocodile clips held in your bare hand
Probes with finger guards and very small bare tips
Bare wire ends twisted onto the terminals

questions.stem: Which is the correct order for safe isolation?
options: Prove dead, switch off, lock off, tag
Switch off, lock off, tag, prove dead
Lock off, tag, switch off, prove dead
Tag, prove dead, switch off, lock off

questions.stem: When you prove a circuit dead, when should the voltage tester be checked on a known live source?
options: Only before the test
Only after the test
Only once a year when it is calibrated
Both before and after the test

questions.stem: Which of these would you look for in a visual inspection?
options: Damaged cables, loose covers and missing labels
The exact voltage measured at every socket outlet
The time a GFCI takes to trip
The current drawn by each appliance

questions.stem: During a visual inspection you find a socket outlet with a cracked cover. What should you do?
options: Ignore it if the socket still works when tested
Tape over the crack to hold it
Record it as a defect to be put right
Paint over the crack to hide it

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to test the continuity of protective conductors?
options: An insulation resistance tester at 500 V
A voltage tester with a lamp
A clamp meter round the cable
A low-resistance ohmmeter

questions.stem: Why do you null (zero) the test leads before a continuity test?
options: To charge the tester battery
So the lead resistance is not added to the reading
To check the insulation on the test leads is sound
To set the tester to 500 V

questions.stem: A continuity test on a protective conductor gives a very high or infinite reading. What does this mean?
options: The conductor is broken or a joint is loose
The conductor is in very good condition
The insulation on the cable is wet and needs drying
The circuit breaker is the wrong size

questions.stem: To test a circuit's protective conductor, the line and protective conductors are linked at the board. Where should the highest reading be found?
options: At the board, next to the link
At the very first socket outlet on the circuit
At the point farthest from the board
At the main earthing terminal

questions.stem: What does the continuity test of the main bonding conductors check?
options: That the water and gas pipes have no leaks
That metal pipes are joined well to the earthing system
That the bonding clamps are painted over neatly and fully
That the pipes are all made of plastic

questions.stem: What test voltage is usually used for an insulation resistance test on 110 V and 220 V circuits?
options: 12 V AC
110 V AC
1000 V AC
500 V DC

questions.stem: Before an insulation resistance test, why are lamps removed and electronic equipment disconnected?
options: They could be damaged or upset the reading
So the room is dark during the test
So that the circuits draw more current during the test
To make the test go much faster

questions.stem: During an insulation resistance test, why should all the light switches be ON?
options: So the lights will come on straight after the test
To save the tester's battery
So all the switched wiring is tested
So the test is quicker

questions.stem: An insulation resistance test gives a high reading in megohms. What does this tell you?
options: There is a short circuit
The protective conductor is broken somewhere
The breaker is too small
The insulation is in good condition

questions.stem: An insulation resistance reading between line and earth is very low. What could be the cause?
options: The cable run is too long for the circuit
Damaged insulation or moisture
The circuit breaker is switched off
The test leads were nulled first

questions.stem: Why must nobody touch the circuit during an insulation resistance test?
options: The tester applies a high voltage that can shock
The circuit will overheat quickly
The tester will lose its calibration and need repair
The reading will be stored wrongly

questions.stem: What can be left in a long cable after an insulation resistance test?
options: A small current that keeps flowing
A magnetic field that stops the breaker
A charge that must be discharged
Heat that damages the insulation

questions.stem: What does a polarity test check?
options: That every cable is the right size for its load
That switches are in the line conductor
That the earth rod is driven deep enough
That the breakers trip quickly

questions.stem: In an Edison screw (ES) lampholder, which conductor must go to the centre contact?
options: The neutral
The earth
None; it is left empty
The line (live)

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous if a light switch is fitted in the neutral instead of the line?
options: The lampholder stays live when the switch is off
The lamp will be much brighter
The circuit breaker will trip as soon as it is on
The switch will wear out faster

questions.stem: How can polarity be checked with the circuit dead?
options: With a voltage tester at each socket
By looking at the colour of the sheath only
With an ohmmeter and a link at the board
By switching on and seeing if the lights work

questions.stem: Which test is done where an installation has its own earth rod?
options: Phase rotation test
Voltage drop test
Lamp brightness test in each room
Earth electrode resistance test

questions.stem: Which test checks that a GFCI (ground fault circuit interrupter) will trip quickly enough?
options: An insulation resistance test at 500 V DC
A GFCI trip test with a suitable tester
A continuity test
A polarity test with an ohmmeter

questions.stem: How often should a user press the test button on a GFCI outlet?
options: Regularly, as the maker's label says
Never, as it damages the device
Only when the power company comes to visit
Only after a lightning storm

questions.stem: Who may carry out live tests, such as earth fault loop impedance, at the Centre?
options: Any trainee who has brought their own tester
The customer, using a plug-in tester
A competent person, with the right instrument
Nobody; live tests are never done

questions.stem: What does an earth fault loop impedance test show?
options: How long each of the cables in the circuit is
If a fault will trip the breaker fast enough
Whether the switches are in the line
How much energy the meter records each month

questions.stem: Where are the test results written down?
options: On the back of the panel door in pencil
On a strip of tape stuck on each of the cables
Nowhere; only faults are noted
On a test results schedule or certificate

questions.stem: During testing you find a fault that could cause a shock. What should you do?
options: Finish every one of the tests first, then decide later
Note it and leave the circuit in use
Make it safe, report it and do not energise it
Tell the customer to fix it later

questions.stem: How do you know whether a test result is acceptable?
options: Compare it with the values the code or maker gives
Ask the customer if it looks right
Accept any reading the meter shows, as it is always right
Use the reading from the last job

questions.stem: Why are older installations inspected and tested from time to time?
options: To use up old test equipment
To make the customer buy all new wiring and fittings
To change the colour of the cables
To find wear and damage before it is dangerous

questions.stem: What should a multimeter be set to before you measure the resistance of an isolated cable?
options: The AC voltage range
The ohms (resistance) range
The current (amps) range for safety
The DC voltage range

questions.stem: Why must test instruments be checked (calibrated) at set times?
options: So they look new
So that the battery lasts much longer between charges
So their readings can be trusted
So the leads stay clean

questions.stem: While you test a circuit, how do you stop others from switching it on?
options: Lock off, tag it and put up warning signs
Ask someone to remember not to touch it
Leave the panel cover off so people can see it is open
Hide the panel key in a drawer

questions.stem: In a visual inspection of the panel, what do you check about each breaker?
options: That it is new and shiny
That it is the same make as the meter
That it trips when tapped with a screwdriver
That its rating suits the cable and the load

questions.stem: In an insulation resistance test on a 110 V circuit, between which conductors is the test made?
options: Only between line and neutral
Between all live conductors, and each to earth
Only between the earth bar and the earth rod outside
Between the meter and the panel

questions.stem: What is a functional test?
options: A test of the cable insulation at 500 V DC
A check of how deep the earth rod is driven
A check that switches and devices work
A count of the sockets in each room

questions.stem: What should you wear when you test in a distribution panel?
options: Safety glasses and insulated boots
Shorts and open sandals to keep cool
A metal watch and rings for good earthing
Wet gloves to get a better grip

questions.stem: After testing is complete and the results are good, what is given to the customer?
options: The tester and its leads
A copy of the certificate and test results
The spare fuses and breakers from the store
A list of the tools used

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the test instrument that can do continuity, insulation, loop and GFCI tests all in one?
What is the name of the small device that gives a known voltage so you can check your voltage tester?
What is the name of the list in a panel that shows each circuit, its breaker and what it supplies?
What do the letters RCD stand for?
Before you switch off a customer's supply to test it, what must you get from the person in charge?
What is the name of the terminal or bar where the earthing conductor and all the bonding conductors meet?
What is the name of the long test lead used to reach from the main earthing terminal to far points in a continuity test?
What fault is it called when the line and neutral conductors touch each other?
What is the name for the inspection and testing of an older installation that is done every few years?
What is the name for the inspection and testing of a new installation before it is first used?
A conductor has a resistance of 0.01 Ω per metre. What is the resistance of 30 m of it, in ohms?
What is the name of the part of a meter that makes a sound when there is continuity?
The meter reads 0.25 Ω with its leads touching. A conductor then reads 0.85 Ω. What is the conductor's real resistance, in ohms?
What is the name of the sudden flash of heat and light that a fault in a panel can cause?

essays.stem: Explain why an installation is inspected and tested, and why the dead tests are always done before any live tests.
essays.modelAnswer: Inspection and testing show that an installation is safe to use and meets the code and the drawings. They find faults such as loose connections, broken earth paths, damaged insulation and wrong connections before anyone can be hurt or a fire can start. They also give a record of the results for the future. The dead tests are done first, with the installation isolated, because they find dangerous faults without any risk from the supply. The continuity test shows that the earth path is sound, so it will be there to protect people when the supply is switched on. The insulation test shows there are no short circuits or earth faults that would cause a dangerous fault current. The polarity test shows that switches and breakers are in the line conductor. If the installation were switched on with these faults, someone could get a shock or the wiring could be damaged. Live tests are done only after the dead tests are passed, by a competent person.
markingPoints: Testing shows the installation is safe and meets the code and drawings
It finds faults before people are hurt, and gives a record
Dead tests find dangerous faults with no risk from the supply
Gives a reason for each dead test (sound earth path, no shorts or earth faults, correct polarity)
Live tests only after dead tests pass, by a competent person

essays.stem: Describe how you would safely isolate a circuit before you test it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would get permission from the person in charge and tell people who use the circuit that the power will be off. I would find the correct breaker from the circuit schedule and switch it off. I would fit a lock to the breaker with a lock-off device so nobody can switch it back on, keep the key with me, and fix a tag with my name, the date and the reason. I would put up a warning sign if needed. Then I would check my voltage tester on a proving unit or a known live source to show that it is working. At the point of work I would test between all the conductors: line and neutral, line and earth, and neutral and earth. When the tester shows no voltage, I would check the tester again on the proving unit, to be sure it did not fail during the test. Only then would I start testing or working, following the Centre's rules.
markingPoints: Gets permission and tells those affected; identifies the correct breaker
Switches off, locks off and keeps the key
Fixes a tag (and signs) with name, date and reason
Checks the tester on a proving unit or known live source before testing
Proves dead between all conductors, then checks the tester again

essays.stem: Describe what you would check during the visual inspection of a new house installation.
essays.modelAnswer: The visual inspection is done with the installation isolated, before testing. At the panel I would check that it is fixed firmly, that each breaker's rating suits its cable and load, that the circuit schedule is filled in, that conductors are the right size and colour, that terminals are tight and that there are no gaps in the cover. I would check that the earthing conductor and main bonding to metal water pipes are in place, with clamps and labels. Around the house I would check that cables are the right type and are supported, protected and not damaged, and that conduit and boxes are secure. Sockets, switches and light fittings should be fixed firmly, with covers not cracked and no bare conductors showing. I would check that GFCI protection is fitted where the rules require it, such as in bathrooms, kitchens and outdoors, and that equipment outdoors is rainproof. I would write down every defect found.
markingPoints: Done with the installation isolated, before the tests
Panel: breaker ratings, schedule, conductor sizes and colours, tight terminals, no gaps
Earthing conductor and main bonding present, with clamps and labels
Cables supported and undamaged; accessories secure with no cracked covers or bare conductors
GFCI protection and rainproof equipment where required; defects recorded

essays.stem: Describe how you would test the continuity of the protective conductor of a radial socket circuit.
essays.modelAnswer: With the circuit isolated, locked off and proved dead, I would set the low-resistance ohmmeter to its lowest ohms range and null the test leads, so their resistance is not added to the reading. At the board I would disconnect the circuit's line conductor from its breaker and link it to the circuit's protective conductor with a short lead. Then I would go to each socket on the circuit and measure between the line terminal and the earth terminal. Every point should give a low reading. The reading should rise a little as I move further from the board, and the highest reading should be at the farthest socket. This reading is the resistance of the line and protective conductors together. I would write it on the test schedule and compare it with the value expected for that cable size and length. A very high or infinite reading means a broken conductor or a loose joint, which must be found and put right. Finally I would remove the link and reconnect the line conductor.
markingPoints: Circuit isolated and proved dead; low-resistance ohmmeter with leads nulled
Links line and protective conductor at the board
Measures line to earth at each point on the circuit
Highest reading at the farthest point, recorded and compared with the expected value
High or infinite reading means a break or loose joint; removes the link afterwards

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare for and carry out an insulation resistance test on a lighting circuit.
essays.modelAnswer: The circuit must be isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead. I would remove the lamps and disconnect any electronic equipment, dimmers or lamps with built-in electronics, because the test voltage could damage them or upset the reading. I would put every switch in the ON position so that all the switched wiring is tested. I would check that nobody is touching the circuit and warn others before I start. I would set the insulation tester to 500 V DC, as is usual for 110 V and 220 V circuits, and check it works. Then I would test between line and neutral, and between line and earth and neutral and earth. Line and neutral can also be linked and tested together to earth. A high reading in megohms shows good insulation; a low reading means damage or moisture. I would let the tester discharge the circuit after each test, then refit the lamps and reconnect equipment, and record the results.
markingPoints: Isolated and proved dead; lamps removed and electronic equipment disconnected
All switches ON so that all wiring is tested
Warns others and checks nobody is touching the circuit
Tests at a suitable voltage (500 V DC) between all conductors and to earth
Explains readings, discharges the circuit, reconnects equipment and records results

essays.stem: Explain what polarity means, why it matters, and how you would test it with the circuit dead.
essays.modelAnswer: Correct polarity means every switch, fuse and single-pole breaker is in the line conductor, the centre contact of an Edison screw lampholder is connected to the line, and socket outlets are wired with line, neutral and earth in the right terminals. It matters because if a switch is in the neutral, the lamp holder is still live when the switch is off, so a person changing a lamp could get a shock. A socket with the line and neutral swapped can make the metal parts of an appliance live. To test with the circuit isolated and proved dead, I would link the line conductor to the protective conductor at the board. Then, with a low-resistance ohmmeter, I would test between the line terminal and earth at each switch, lampholder and socket, with switches ON. A low reading shows the line is in the right place. I would also check that the neutral does not give this reading. I would remove the link and record the results.
markingPoints: Defines correct polarity: switches and protective devices in the line; ES centre contact to line; sockets correct
Explains the danger of wrong polarity, such as a live lampholder when switched off
Circuit isolated and proved dead; line linked to protective conductor at the board
Tests with an ohmmeter at each point, switches ON; low reading confirms line
Removes the link and records the results

essays.stem: Explain how you would choose, check and look after the test instruments you use for inspection and testing.
essays.modelAnswer: I would choose the right instrument for each test: a voltage tester and proving unit for proving dead, a low-resistance ohmmeter for continuity, an insulation resistance tester for insulation, and an earth resistance tester for an earth rod. A multifunction tester can do many of these. Before use I would check the case is not cracked, the battery is good and the calibration date has not passed. I would check the leads and probes for damage, and use probes with finger guards and small bare tips, and fused leads where the maker says. I would do a quick check, such as touching the leads together for continuity, to see that the instrument works. After use I would switch it off, clean it, coil the leads loosely and store it in its case, dry and away from heat. Any damage or wrong reading would be reported, and the instrument kept out of use until it is repaired and checked.
markingPoints: Chooses the right instrument for each test
Checks case, battery and calibration date before use
Checks leads and probes; uses guarded probes and fused leads
Does a quick function check before testing
Stores it properly after use and reports damage, keeping it out of use

essays.stem: A test result on a new circuit is not acceptable. Describe what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would not switch the circuit on, and I would keep it isolated, locked off and tagged. I would check that the result is real: that the instrument is working, the leads were nulled, the right range was used and the test was set up correctly, then repeat the test. If the result is still bad, I would find the fault by testing in sections, for example by splitting the circuit at a junction box or socket and testing each half, until the faulty part is found. For a low insulation reading I would look for damaged cable, a nail or screw through a cable, water in a box or equipment left connected. For a high continuity reading I would look for a loose or missing connection. I would report the fault to my supervisor, put it right as agreed, then repeat the tests in the correct order. Both the fault and the new results would be written on the test record.
markingPoints: Does not energise; keeps the circuit isolated, locked off and tagged
Checks the instrument and set-up, then repeats the test
Finds the fault by testing in sections and looking for likely causes
Reports to the supervisor and puts the fault right
Retests in the correct order and records the fault and the new results

essays.stem: Explain the purpose of the earth fault loop impedance test and the GFCI test, and when and by whom they are done.
essays.modelAnswer: The earth fault loop impedance test measures the resistance of the whole path a fault current would take: from the supply, through the line conductor to the fault, back through the protective conductor and the earthing to the supply. If this is low enough, a fault will draw a large current and the breaker will trip quickly, before anyone is harmed. The GFCI test checks that a ground fault circuit interrupter trips when a small current leaks to earth, and that it trips fast enough to protect a person from a serious shock. The test button is also pressed to check the mechanism. Both tests need the supply to be on, so they are done only after the visual inspection and all the dead tests have been passed and the installation has been safely connected. They are carried out by a competent person, using the right instrument as its maker says and following the Centre's rules. Results are recorded on the test schedule.
markingPoints: Loop test measures the fault path impedance so the breaker will trip fast
GFCI test checks it trips on a small leakage current, quickly enough to protect people
Both need the supply on, so they are done only after the inspection and dead tests are passed
Done by a competent person with the right instrument, following the rules
Results recorded

essays.stem: Describe how you would record the results of inspection and testing, and hand over the installation.
essays.modelAnswer: As I do each test, I write the result straight onto the test results schedule for that circuit, with the instrument used and the date, rather than trying to remember it later. For each circuit I record the circuit number and what it supplies, the breaker type and rating, the cable size, the continuity reading, the insulation resistance readings and whether polarity is correct. I also record the earth electrode result and any live test results done by the competent person. I compare every result with the value the code or maker gives and mark any that are not acceptable. Defects found in the visual inspection are listed. When everything is acceptable, the certificate is completed and signed by the person responsible. I would make sure the circuit schedule in the panel is correct. At handover I give the customer a copy of the certificate and results, explain where the main breaker is and how to test the GFCI outlets, and keep a copy on file.
markingPoints: Records each result at once on the test schedule, with date and instrument
Records the right details for each circuit (breaker, cable, readings, polarity)
Compares results with expected values and lists defects
Certificate completed and signed; panel schedule correct
Gives the customer a copy, explains the main breaker and GFCI test, keeps a copy

practical1.title: Visual inspection and continuity testing of a training board installation
practical1.brief: The instructor gives the group a training board wired with one lighting circuit and one socket circuit, with some defects set on purpose. The board is isolated, locked off and tagged, and it stays dead for the whole task. First, show safe isolation: switch off, lock off, tag, and prove dead with a voltage tester that is checked on the proving unit before and after. Then carry out a visual inspection of the board with the inspection checklist, and list every defect found. Next, null the low-resistance ohmmeter and test the continuity of the protective conductors of both circuits, linking line and protective conductor at the board and testing at each point. Record all results on the test schedule. Every member does one part of the isolation, inspects one area of the board and makes at least two continuity readings, which another member records. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group with the completed checklist and schedule.
materials: Training board with a lighting circuit and a socket circuit (not connected to a supply)
Lock-off device, padlock and danger tag
Low-resistance ohmmeter with leads, wander lead and a short linking lead
Visual inspection checklist and test results schedule
photos: The board locked off and tagged
The tester being checked on the proving unit before and after proving dead
The completed visual inspection checklist, with defects listed
The link fitted at the board between line and protective conductor
A continuity reading being taken at the farthest point, showing the display
checklist: Carried out safe isolation in the right order, with the tester checked before and after
Inspected their area carefully and found the defects set in it
Recorded defects clearly on the checklist
Nulled the test leads before the continuity test
Fitted the link correctly and tested at each point
Recorded readings correctly and found the highest at the farthest point
Removed the link and left the board as found
Used the instruments as the maker says and returned them safely
safety: The training board is never connected to a supply during this task
Use only test leads and probes that are in good condition, with finger guards
Keep the lock and tag on until the instructor ends the task
Follow the instrument maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Insulation resistance and polarity testing of a training board installation
practical2.brief: The instructor gives the group a training board wired with a lighting circuit (with an Edison screw lampholder) and a socket circuit, with one or two faults set on purpose. The board is isolated, locked off and tagged, and it stays dead for the whole task. Show safe isolation first. Then prepare the circuits for the insulation resistance test: remove lamps, disconnect any electronic device and put all switches ON. Warn the group, then test at 500 V DC between all conductors and from each to earth, as the instructor shows. Next, test the polarity of each switch, lampholder and socket with an ohmmeter and a link at the board. Find the set faults, write them on the test schedule and say how each should be put right. Every member makes at least one insulation reading and one polarity check, and each takes a turn recording. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group with the completed schedule.
materials: Training board with a lighting circuit and a socket circuit (not connected to a supply)
Lock-off device, padlock, danger tag, voltage tester and proving unit
Low-resistance ohmmeter with a short linking lead
Test results schedule and a fault report sheet
photos: The board locked off and tagged, and the tester checked before and after proving dead
The circuits prepared: lamps removed, electronic devices disconnected, switches ON
An insulation resistance reading between line and earth, showing the display
The link at the board for the polarity test
A polarity check at the Edison screw lampholder centre contact
The completed test results schedule, with the faults found
The board restored as found, and the instruments put away
checklist: Carried out safe isolation in the right order, with the tester checked before and after
Prepared the circuit correctly before the insulation test
Warned others and did not touch the circuit during the test
Tested insulation resistance between the right conductors at the right voltage
Tested polarity at each switch, lampholder and socket
Found the set faults and gave a correct way to put each right
Restored the board and returned the instruments safely
safety: The training board is never connected to a supply during this task
The insulation tester gives a high test voltage: warn others and keep hands clear during each test
Let the tester discharge the circuit before you touch it
Use only leads and probes in good condition, with finger guards
Follow the instrument maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
